lesson_title: Queues Under Ceilings, Piles on Floors: the State in the Market
hook_text: Cap the price of cooking oil and the oil VANISHES. Here's the mechanism.
clip_script: The CEILING: the state presses the price DOWN below its resting point — cooking oil capped cheap during a shortage crisis. Shoppers cheer and pour in; but watch the producers: at the capped price, pressing and bottling oil barely pays, so they produce LESS. Many wanting, few supplying: the shelves go bare. And here is the cruel mechanism: the price is not ALLOWED to rise and call more oil in — that is now illegal. So who gets the cheap oil? Whoever queued from dawn. Whoever knows the shop owner. And behind the shop, someone sells bottles quietly at DOUBLE — the black market, born in the space between what the law permits and what the shelves hold. Cheap oil for some, no oil for many, dear oil in the shadows. A ceiling makes QUEUES. Flip it: hold a potato price UP and growers plant every field while buyers take fewer bags — the warehouse fills and the state buys the mountain. A floor makes PILES.
visual_style: A shop scene: price tag stamped down, shelves draining bottle by bottle, a dawn queue snaking round the block; a shadowed back-door handoff; then a warehouse filling with potato sacks into a mountain; closing split-frame of queue-under-ceiling and pile-on-floor.
mood: Cautionary fable energy — vivid, even-handed, non-partisan.
pacing: Rapid cause-and-effect beats, symmetrical flip to the floor, clean two-line landing.
